name: codex-manager
description: Manage Codex across connected PCs from your browser: remote sessions, files, Git, terminals, accounts, quota, task boards, and Auto Resume.

codexManager.codexAppRestartMode.markdownDescription: Restart the running desktop app automatically or ask each time.

codexManager.codexAppRestartEnabled.markdownDescription: Manage desktop app restarts after account switches.

codexManager.dashboardTheme.markdownDescription: Choose a dashboard theme; `auto` follows VS Code.

codexManager.systemInfoEnabled.markdownDescription: Show System Info in Account Center and the system picker: battery, network, CPU, RAM, disk space, and uptime when available.

codexManager.privacyMode.markdownDescription: Hide account identities in all dashboards and account details.

codexManager.displayLanguage.markdownDescription: Choose the language for Codex Manager.

codexManager.autoRefreshMinutes.markdownDescription: Check all account quotas every N minutes; `0` turns polling off and `1`â€“`4` use `5`.

codexManager.autoRefreshCurrentMinutes.markdownDescription: Check current account quota every N minutes; `0` turns polling off.

codexManager.tokenHistoryRetentionDays.markdownDescription: Legacy setting retained for compatibility. Verified VS Code usage is kept in SQLite across account removal; chart queries load only the selected date window.

codexManager.dailyTokenUsageIntervalMinu.markdownDescription: Minimum minutes between automatic token history checks; server retry delays still apply.

codexManager.dailyTokenUsageEnabled.markdownDescription: Save daily usage at the selected interval and fill missing chart history; saved usage stays when off.

codexManager.usageHistoryRetentionDays.markdownDescription: Legacy setting retained for compatibility. New quota history is not recorded.

codexManager.codexModuleEnabled.markdownDescription: Enable the optional Codex session module. Use Settings > Workspace > Session modules > Codex to verify an existing runtime or download it separately before enabling.

codexManager.claudeModuleEnabled.markdownDescription: Enable the optional Claude session module. Use Settings > Workspace > Session modules > Claude to verify an existing runtime or download it separately before enabling.

codexManager.cliIntegrationEnabled.markdownDescription: Workspace: add chats and terminals to the dashboard.

codexManager.apiAccessEnabled.markdownDescription: Allow generated Bearer tokens to call the local dashboard API.

codexManager.mcpAutoSetupEnabled.markdownDescription: Automatically register Codex Manager MCP for new Codex sessions. First setup enables the local dashboard API and creates a workspace-operation token. Existing user-managed or disabled MCP entries are preserved.

codexManager.workspaceTextFileLimitMb.markdownDescription: Maximum text file size in MB for the workspace editor, used for opening and saving files.

codexManager.workspaceFileLimitMb.markdownDescription: Maximum size in MB for connected-folder files, saved workspace files, and Office documents. Chat uploads remain capped at 100 MB per message.

codexManager.autoSwitchEnabled.markdownDescription: Switch accounts when current quota reaches either configured limit.

codexManager.modelCapacityAutoSwitchEnab.markdownDescription: Switch to another verified capable account after consecutive model-capacity failures, only when no other session is running. Standalone retries verified capacity interruptions with bounded backoff when Auto Resume permits. Requires Auto Switch.

codexManager.modelCapacityFailureCount.markdownDescription: Consecutive model-capacity failures before switching accounts. Failures while another session is running do not count.

codexManager.standaloneCapacityRetryDela.markdownDescription: Initial standalone retry delay after a verified capacity interruption. Later retries back off exponentially.

codexManager.autoSwitchWaitForSessionsEn.markdownDescription: Wait for running chats before automatic switches or resets; manual switching stays available.

codexManager.autoSwitchReloadWindowEnabl.markdownDescription: Automatically reload VS Code after an account switch changes the active account.

codexManager.autoResumeEnabled.markdownDescription: With Auto Switch on, recover unfinished parent chats after restart, using official Codex tabs in VS Code or private turns in standalone. Also permits bounded standalone capacity retries. Per-session overrides apply; paused goals stay paused.

codexManager.crossWindowAccountModeEnabl.markdownDescription: Experimental: use a separate account in each VS Code window.

codexManager.autoSwitchHourlyThreshold.markdownDescription: Switch when remaining 5-hour quota reaches this percentage or less.

codexManager.autoSwitchWeeklyThreshold.markdownDescription: Switch when remaining weekly or monthly quota reaches this percentage or less.

codexManager.autoSwitchRefreshAllBeforeS.markdownDescription: Check enabled account quotas before alerts or automatic switches.

codexManager.autoResetEnabled.markdownDescription: Use an available reset credit when every enabled account is out of quota.

codexManager.autoResetWeeklyThreshold.markdownDescription: Use a reset credit when weekly or monthly quota reaches this percentage or less.

codexManager.autoSwitchLockMinutes.markdownDescription: Keep the current account for this many minutes; `0` disables the default lock.

codexManager.codexAppPath.markdownDescription: Choose the desktop app location or leave empty for auto-detect.

codexManager.codexCliPath.markdownDescription: Choose the Codex program or leave empty for auto-detect.

codexManager.quotaWarningEnabled.markdownDescription: Warn when current account quota falls below either configured limit.

codexManager.quotaWarningThreshold.markdownDescription: Warn below this percentage of remaining 5-hour quota.

codexManager.quotaWarningWeeklyThreshold.markdownDescription: Warn below this percentage of remaining weekly or monthly quota.

codexManager.quotaGreenThreshold.markdownDescription: Show green from this percentage of remaining quota.

codexManager.quotaYellowThreshold.markdownDescription: Show yellow from this percentage until green; lower values appear red.

codexManager.encryptedSyncEnabled.markdownDescription: Share encrypted account reservations between PCs.

codexManager.fullCrossPcAccountSyncEnabl.markdownDescription: Share encrypted account sessions and tokens between PCs; off keeps logins local.

codexManager.webDashboardEnabled.markdownDescription: Open a browser dashboard on this PC; set a shared password before allowing remote access.

codexManager.webSocketServerEnabled.markdownDescription: Connect systems through the configured shared dashboard server.

codexManager.alwaysActive.markdownDescription: Keep the local dashboard, session queue, and automation services running after VS Code closes. Runs as a standalone local Node host using the same dashboard port and requires a shared dashboard password.

codexManager.alwaysActiveStartWithSystem.markdownDescription: Start the local dashboard host at Windows boot or sign-in, or at macOS user sign-in. Separate from Always Active. Windows needs administrator permission for a pre-sign-in boot task; macOS installs a per-user LaunchAgent without sudo for the next sign-in.

codexManager.cloudflaredDomain.markdownDescription: Optional HTTPS dashboard address for other PCs; set a shared password before sharing.

codexManager.officeWorkspaceRoot.markdownDescription: Root folder for isolated office user workspaces. Users receive a folder below this path.

codexManager.teamWorkspaceEnabled.markdownDescription: Enable Team workspace sign-in and role-gated Team routes.

codexManager.officeDatabaseProvider.markdownDescription: Office user data store. PostgreSQL automatically migrates users, conversations, logs and workspace records once. Master data stays local; connection failures do not fall back to SQLite.

codexManager.officePostgresUrl.markdownDescription: PostgreSQL connection URL for office data. Keep credentials in a protected machine setting.

codexManager.encryptedSyncClaimAllAccoun.markdownDescription: Reserve every enabled account for this PC; off reserves only the current account.

codexManager.encryptedSyncVsCodeHeartbea.markdownDescription: Choose the minimum interval between VS Code Settings Sync saves.

codexManager.officeMaxActiveRequests.markdownDescription: Maximum simultaneous user workspace assistant requests. Additional requests stay queued.

codexManager.officeGlobalPrompt.default:
Deliver the highest practical quality for every request. Aim for a 10/10 result in accuracy, completeness, usefulness, clarity and presentation, judged against the user's actual goal. Match effort to the task and the user's constraints; quality does not require long answers, unnecessary tools or extra features. Never promise perfection or award yourself a quality score as a substitute for evidence.

Understand and complete the work. Establish the requested outcome, audience, format and relevant constraints from the conversation and available sources. Treat the request as authorization to perform the necessary work within its scope and the granted workspace permissions. Automatically proceed with authorized actions and routine implementation or design choices; do not ask for repeated permission, a generic approval or a go-ahead. Ask only when an essential answer, genuine user choice or required authorization is missing. When a question is necessary, always show it through request_user_input with clear concise options when meaningful, and wait for the user's answer; never silently choose an answer to a question the user must resolve. Otherwise state important assumptions and proceed. For substantial multi-step work, show a concise plan, carry out the authorized work and keep progress truthful. Do not stop at an outline, instructions or an offer to continue when the user requested a finished deliverable. Respect scope, permissions, ownership and current file revisions. Preserve original data and user work; this instruction does not grant access or authorize unrelated, destructive or external actions outside the request.

Choose tools and skills deliberately. Before specialized work, check the available skill catalog and automatically load the relevant workspace skills with use_office_skill; do not wait for the user to name or approve them. Include visual-design and the matching document or presentation skill for visual deliverables, spreadsheet-workbooks and spreadsheet-formulas for Excel tasks, data-analysis for analytical work, interface-design for interface refinement, and fact-checking for material factual claims as appropriate. Combine complementary skills when useful, and skip irrelevant workflows. Inspect the capabilities actually available in this conversation. Prefer tools that can create the requested format with the needed control, editability and verification. Discover assigned connections when they may contain the required data. Do not assume that a plugin installed elsewhere, a skill description or a library name grants tools, execution or access. If a route is inadequate, try a supported better route within the user's authorization. Explain any remaining limitation before representing the result as complete; do not silently substitute formats or claim a basic output meets an advanced design brief.

Use Elephant-Goldfish when appropriate and available for complex planning, substantial deliverables or changes that benefit from independent review. The Elephant preserves the goal and builds a coherent solution; the Goldfish independently checks the result against the requirements with fresh context, identifies material defects and verifies fixes. Apply an available EGM workflow within the user's authorization; do not introduce repeated approval prompts for already authorized work. A true Goldfish review requires an actual independent reviewer capability; never present an ordinary self-check as an independent review. When that capability is absent, perform the self-check below and disclose the distinction only when relevant. Do not force this workflow on simple questions.

Ground factual work in evidence. Use current primary sources for changing, technical or high-stakes claims when the relevant tools are available. Read the supporting material and cite exact sources near the claims. Separate verified facts, assumptions, estimates and recommendations. Check dates, units, formulas, totals and denominators as applicable. Never invent data, citations, quotations, test results, preview URLs or completed actions. Keep private information out of public searches and unrelated connections. Explain uncertainty and unavailable verification plainly. For substantive factual replies, load fact-checking when available and apply a final evidence check: detect unsupported assertions, contradictions, stale information, misleading comparisons and sources that do not support the claim. Correct or omit unsupported assertions, or clearly qualify them when they matter to the user's decision. Retain credible conflicting evidence and distinguish it from speculation. Do not claim to have fact-checked live information when the required sources or tools were unavailable.

Design deliverables for their audience. Use a coherent visual direction, readable typography, strong hierarchy, consistent alignment and spacing, accessible contrast and purposeful visuals. Choose charts, comparisons, timelines, diagrams or imagery when they communicate the evidence better than paragraphs. Preserve editable text and charts where supported. Avoid repetitive title-and-bullet layouts, decoration without meaning, tiny text and superficial recolouring presented as a redesign. Use the requested format; discuss a supported alternative if tools cannot meet it.

Check your own work before every delivery. Re-read the request and compare the complete result with every material requirement. Check reasoning, factual support, calculations, missing content, consistency, language and practical usability. For files, create and read back the actual output, verify its format and contents, and render and inspect its visual layout when the available tools support it. For code or interactive work, run the relevant checks and exercise the affected behavior when possible. Fix material defects, repeat affected checks after changes and stop when the requirements are met with no known material defect. If a check fails, times out or is unavailable, preserve the failure and explain what remains unverified; never claim an unperformed check passed or call an outline a rendered preview. A concise answer still needs an accuracy and completeness check.

Users access their work only through User Workspace, including its Browser and Files panels. They do not have access to the server desktop, terminal, or physical folders. After creating or updating a deliverable, always provide a clickable Markdown link with its workspace-relative path, for example [Open report](reports/report.txt), plus a download link such as [Download report](reports/report.txt?download=1). URL-encode spaces and special characters in link destinations. For websites, provide a verified reachable URL that opens in a tab on the user device by default. Keep localhost links in the workspace Browser and explain that localhost refers to the workspace server, not the user device. When AI interaction needs the workspace Browser, mark the Markdown link with the title workspace-browser. For a saved HTML website, call open_preview to open it in the right panel Browser tab and link to the HTML file as Open preview. Inline styles and scripts are supported; server applications require an isolated execution service. Offer a download as well; do not claim a server is running. Use supplied tools and confirmed files only. Keep explanations practical and avoid physical paths, internal tool output, and instructions that require direct server access.

Deliver clearly. Lead with the answer or completed result, use plain language and match the user's requested language and tone. Keep detail proportional to the decision or task. For substantial work, briefly state what was delivered, what was verified and any material remaining limitation. Surface failure or partial completion instead of hiding it. Do not describe work as professional, polished, fully tested or finished beyond the evidence you actually have.
codexManager.officeGlobalPrompt.markdownDescription: Global guidance applied to every User Workspace conversation. Does not affect master workspace sessions.

codexManager.officeDefaultSkills.markdownDescription: Corporate skills enabled by default for User Workspace conversations.

codexManager.officeAutoPresentation.markdownDescription: Allow the assistant to show relevant permitted project panels in User Workspace.

codexManager.officeSessionRetentionDays.markdownDescription: Number of days to retain deleted User Workspace conversations and session files for support before permanent cleanup.

codexManager.officeDefaultModel.markdownDescription: Default model for new User Workspace chats. Users may select another model. Leave empty to require users to choose.

codexManager.officeModelMode.markdownDescription: Use manual model selection or automatic Regular, Professional and Expert profiles in User Workspace.

codexManager.officeRouterModel.markdownDescription: Lightweight model used to select an automatic User Workspace profile and thinking level.

codexManager.officeRegularModel.markdownDescription: Backend model for the Regular User Workspace profile.

codexManager.officeProfessionalModel.markdownDescription: Backend model for the Professional User Workspace profile.

codexManager.officeExpertModel.markdownDescription: Backend model for the Expert User Workspace profile.

codexManager.officeProfilePicker.markdownDescription: Allow User Workspace users to choose Auto, Regular, Professional or Expert. Turn off to lock Auto.

codexManager.officePresentation.markdownDescription: User Workspace assistant identity, welcome text, mode labels and contextual card catalog. Edit from Master workspace settings.

codexManager.officeServices.markdownDescription: Optional User Workspace renderer, isolated execution service and web-search credentials. Configure in master workspace settings. Keys stay on this host.

codexManager.codexFallbackModelIds.markdownDescription: Editable Codex fallback model IDs, one per line, used when live discovery is unavailable. Successful live discovery replaces this list with the models actually returned. Save an empty list to clear every fallback; Load models rebuilds it. Fallback entries do not confirm account access.
